Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

speaker noun

a person who speaks

also public speaker, the person speaking, who’s speaking?, orator, spokesman

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.213 (Lewis & Short): hunc ego appellō ōrātōrem
Liv. 1.15 (Lewis & Short): envoys sent to sue for peace

ōrātor, ōrātōris m.

noun, third declension

a (public) speaker, orator; spokesman

One who speaks in public, in court or before an assembly, and so the trained orator; in early Latin and Livy also an envoy who carries a spoken message (Lewis & Short). Not the person who happens to be talking.

Other words

  • is quī loquitur (dīcit) — the speaker, the person speaking

    phrase: a relative clause · classical · Plaut. Curc. 229: Quis hic est quī loquitur?

    Latin names the person by what they are doing: quī loquitur, the one talking; quī dīcit, the one making a speech. A speaker of Latin is quī Latīnē loquitur (see speak a language).

  • locūtor, locūtōris m. — a speaker; a chatterer

    noun, third declension · avoid · post-classical · Apul. M. 1 (Lewis & Short): rudis locūtor exōticī sermōnis; Gell. 1.15.1 (Lewis & Short)

    Post-classical and rare: in Apuleius a speaker of a language, in Gellius a babbler (Lewis & Short). Use quī loquitur.

Examples

  • Quis hic loquitur? Mysis? salvē.

    Who’s that speaking? Mysis? Hello.Ter. And. 267

  • Quis hic est quī loquitur?

    Who is that speaking?Plaut. Curc. 229

See also talk, say, speak, speaker, address.
